articles.title: 700 supermarkets hit, millions lost: France warns cyberattacks on refrigeration systems may still be ongoing
articles.summary: France's cybersecurity authority has warned that a cyberattack targeting refrigeration systems at supermarkets may still be underway, as stores restock
articles.body: France's cybersecurity authority has warned that a cyberattack targeting refrigeration systems at supermarkets may still be underway, as stores restock fresh and frozen goods discarded after temperatures inside refrigerators and freezers surged.The agency said on Tuesday night that the attacks were “likely still underway” and urged retailers to reconnect refrigeration systems to the internet only through secure virtual private network (VPN) connections or protected networks.It also advised stores to install firmware updates and change passwords, according to the news agency Associated Press (AP).Attackers remotely took control of refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets and independent stores across France in the early hours of Monday. Temperatures reportedly reached 50 degrees Celsius for around six hours, forcing retailers to dispose of fresh and frozen products.The Intermarché supermarket chain reported losses of “tens of millions of euros” in a single day.French finance minister Roland Lescure said around 700 of the country's 10,000 supermarkets had been affected, describing the incident as a “wake-up call for everyone”.The attack has also raised concerns about the security of connected refrigeration equipment and the potential impact of cyber incidents on food supply chains.Older refrigeration systems under scrutinyFrance's cybersecurity agency said it was aware of numerous compromises involving remote-control modules used in refrigeration systems manufactured by Danish company Danfoss and US-based Copeland.Danfoss said many of the affected systems were older products that no longer received software or security updates. Copeland said a vulnerability had been identified in “a discontinued, end-of-life generation of controllers” and that it was working with affected customers.A report published in August by US cybersecurity firm Claroty identified vulnerabilities in the Danfoss AK-SM 800A and Copeland XWeb Pro platforms, which are used to manage refrigeration infrastructure in supermarkets, warehouses and other facilities. Claroty said some Danfoss controllers were directly accessible through the public internet, potentially exposing them to attacks. The vulnerabilities identified in the report have since been fixed.Reuters quoted cybersecurity experts as saying the French attack appeared to have exploited weaknesses in older systems and inadequate security practices. The precise method used to gain control of the refrigeration equipment has not been publicly disclosed.Ken Munro, a partner at British cybersecurity firm Pen Test Partners, described the issue as one of basic cyber hygiene.“This is about basic cyber hygiene,” he said. “Get it wrong and you get a smelly mess of defrosted food.”A scan using the internet search service Shodan found at least 4,500 Danfoss interfaces still visible online on Tuesday. It was not independently established how many were running vulnerable software.Dutch supermarket chain resumes systems after separate incidentMeanwhile, Dutch supermarket chain Albert Heijn was restocking shelves on Wednesday as its parent company, Ahold Delhaize, began restarting systems that had been shut down as a precaution following a separate cybersecurity incident.The incident, which began on Sunday evening, disrupted online services, halted home deliveries and affected some supplies to the retailer's extensive network of stores in the Netherlands.The Dutch National Cybersecurity Centre said several cyber incidents had affected Europe's food sector but saw “no reason at this time to believe that these incidents are linked”.The disruption highlighted the dependence of supermarkets on digital systems and frequent deliveries. Pieter Zwaan, a senior researcher at the Clingendael Institute, told AP that Dutch supermarkets relied on “just in time” deliveries several times a day to keep shelves stocked.“Without IT and electricity it is impossible to order and deliver product to supermarkets” so frequently, he said.Investigations underway, no perpetrators identifiedAuthorities in France and the Netherlands are investigating the incidents. Europol confirmed to AP that it was in contact with authorities in the affected countries but declined to provide further details because the investigation was ongoing.No perpetrators have been publicly identified, and no group has claimed responsibility for the French attack.François Deruty, a former operations director at the French Cybersecurity Agency who now works as chief intelligence officer at cybersecurity company Sekoia, said it remained unclear whether the attack was directed by an organised actor or carried out by an individual.“I still can't determine whether it's being directed by someone or whether it's an individual trying to take advantage of the prevailing chaos to show off their skills or send a message,” Deruty said.He added that the timing was notable, as French politicians were already dealing with several issues and the disruption had a direct impact on everyday life.The French government has said the attack did not threaten the country's overall food supplies, although Lescure acknowledged that it “touches the heart of our food security”.You use AI every day. articles.title: 3 Indians killed in Germany fire, 5 injured; resident arrested on murder suspicion
articles.summary: At least three Indians were killed and five others injured after a fire broke out at a residential building in Bochum, Germany, early Tuesday, local media
articles.body: At least three Indians were killed and five others injured after a fire broke out at a residential building in Bochum, Germany, early Tuesday, local media reported on Wednesday. Police have arrested a 41-year-old resident on suspicion of murder as investigators probe whether the blaze was deliberately started.The victims were two women aged 25 and 27, and a 26-year-old man, German public broadcaster WDR reported, citing Bochum police. Their identities and home states in India have not been disclosed.The five injured people suffered smoke inhalation and were taken to hospitals in Bochum. Their nationalities have not been reported.Police suspect arsonPolice and prosecutors announced the arrest on Wednesday. The suspect is a 41-year-old Romanian national, German news channel n-tv reported, citing the German Press Agency (DPA).A Bochum police spokesperson told WDR that there were initial grounds to suspect the man of murder. He was questioned by officers from the homicide squad.Investigators have ruled out a technical defect as the cause of the fire and suspect arson. However, they are still examining whether the blaze was deliberately set or started accidentally.Flames hamper rescueThe fire broke out at around 4.15 am local time on Tuesday in a multi-family residential building in the Hofstede district of Bochum, prompting emergency services to respond.Firefighters found the three victims dead inside an apartment on the second floor. articles.title: New York City to ban iconic horse-drawn carriages from June 1, 2028; decision comes after Indian tourist Romanch Mahajan's death
articles.summary: An Indian family's New York vacation turned into a nightmare on June 17, when 18-year-old Romanch Mahajan died after falling from a horse-drawn carriage
articles.body: An Indian family's New York vacation turned into a nightmare on June 17, when 18-year-old Romanch Mahajan died after falling from a horse-drawn carriage in Central Park in an attempt to save his mother Priya Mahajan who fell from the carriage first. The carriage driver briefly stepped away to take a photograph when the family was inside the carriage. The horse suddenly bolted in the absence of the driver nd Romanch's mother fell. Romanch immediately jumped from the moving carriage and suffered a fatal head injury. He later died at New York-Presbyterian Weill Cornell Medical center.Romanch's parents appealed to the administration to ban horse-drawn carriages so that no other family has to go through what they did. A bill was drafted to ban horse carriages in NYC and it was named after the Indian teen -- Romanch's law. The bill is now expected to be brought to the council floor for a voter later this month. Mayor Zohran Mamdani and City Council Speaker Julie Menin reached a deal on the legislation.The ban will be implemented in phases and will take effect on June 1, 2028.“The tragic and preventable death of 18-year-old Romanch Mahajan made clear that the status quo is no longer acceptable,” Menin said in a statement. “Horse drawn carriages have long been part of New York City’s history, but in an increasingly busy Central Park, this tradition has become a growing public safety liability. Next week, the Council will take decisive action by voting on Romanch’s Law to protect New Yorkers, visitors, and the horses themselves.”What will happen to these horses, drivers and the owners?The bill has provisions requiring the horse owners to notify the Mayor's Office of Animal Welfare before disposing of the animals. The bill prohibits the owners from selling the horses or to transfer them for slaughter of for use in another horse-drawn business. For drivers, the bill has industry transition framework in which the NYC council will have to come up with a plan to help these workers transition into new jobs. They will be trained through other agencies, including the NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission, the MTA, NYC Transit, the Port Authority and hospitality and tourism industries, where they will eventually get jobs.Transport Workers Union International President John Samuelsen said there is no meaningful economic relied for the workers. articles.title: Netflix to shed 1,000 jobs in steepest cuts since 2022
articles.summary: The cuts equate to around 6% of the streaming giant's total workforce worldwide.
articles.body:
Netflix has said it will cut 1,000 jobs globally as the streaming giant faces competition from rivals.

The cuts - the steepest since 2022 - will mainly affect its human resources, legal, product and technology teams and equates to around 6% of its total workforce.

Last month, Netflix 's co-chief executive, Ted Sarandos, told the Bloomberg Screentime summit that the company was "not growing as fast as I want us to".

The streaming industry is going through a period of consolidation following Paramount's $110bn (£83.6bn) merger with Warner Bros, the owner of HBO, while free platforms such as YouTube and TikTok continue to attract viewers.

In an email to staff, Sarandos and co-chief executive Greg Peters said Netflix would "continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation".

Netflix had come close to its own deal with Warner Bros but was outbid in the end by Paramount .

Commenting on the "organisational changes", Sarandos and Peters said: "Our mission - to entertain the world - is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritise our people and resources."

Managers will tell employees whether their job has been cut "soon".

The email added that the firm was on track to meet its financial forecasts. The streaming service is due to report its latest results on 20 October.

Investors have been weighing up user engagement - the amount of time customers spend on Netflix - as it competes with platforms such as YouTube and TikTok.

The firm has continued to commission shows - its most popular at the moment is "Below", an underwater mystery series.

It has also been attempting to expand its business, including gaming and allowing adverts to play before and during shows and films.

However, "they haven't been able to find another line of major revenue," said Ross Benes, senior analyst at eMarketer.

He added that the company remains reliant on a subscription business that could be approaching a plateau.

"Eventually, because they're nearing a ceiling with that, they'll need another revenue stream to diversify, and that's where it's been more of a struggle," he said.

The last major redundancy round at Netflix was in 2022, when it cut about 450 jobs after losing subscribers for the first time in more than a decade.

articles.title: Wisconsin plane crash kills 5 adults, child as authorities probe final communications with air traffic control
articles.summary: A Piper PA-46 crashed in a wooded area in Sauk County, Wisconsin Tuesday night, killing all six people aboard including a child. The FAA is investigating.
articles.body: A small plane carrying five adults and a child was in contact with air traffic control before crashing into a wooded area in Wisconsin Tuesday night, killing everyone aboard and leaving investigators searching for answers about the aircraft's final moments. The Piper PA-46 was on a return flight from Kenosha to Menomonie when it went down in the Town of Dellona in Sauk County, according to the Sauk County Sheriff's Office. Authorities received multiple reports of a downed aircraft around 9:31 p.m. Tuesday and dispatched emergency crews to the area of Park Lane, where first responders discovered the wreckage in a densely wooded area west of Herwig Road. SMALL PLANE CRASHES INTO SHALLOW WATER NEAR REMOTE ALASKA TOWN, KILLING ALL 4 PEOPLE ABOARD Rescue crews began searching for survivors while investigators worked to identify the aircraft and determine how many people were aboard. All six occupants were ultimately found dead at the scene, authorities said. Their identities have not been released. Investigators are now working to determine what communications took place between the aircraft and a nearby air traffic control tower before the crash, as well as whether weather conditions in the area may have played a role. "We know that they had contact with the tower prior to the crash and investigators are looking into that today to find out what that communication was," Sauk County Sheriff Chip Meister told FOX6 Milwaukee. FATHER, SON KILLED IN PLANE CRASH ON WAY HOME FROM BASEBALL GAME Meister said it remained unclear who owned the aircraft but confirmed that it was not a commercial plane. No structures were damaged, and no injuries were reported on the ground, according to the sheriff's office. The crash site remained secured Wednesday as investigators worked to piece together the circumstances surrounding the deadly flight. articles.title: US Social Security benefits to rise by 3.6 percent in 2027
articles.summary: Retired Americans will see a $75 boost in monthly cheques as benefits rise amid widespread inflation challenges.
articles.body:
United States Social Security benefits will increase by 3.6 percent beginning in 2027, marking one of the largest cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) of the decade.

On Wednesday, the Social Security Administration announced the hike after the Bureau of Labor Statistics published the Consumer Price Index for September. The alteration represents a four-year high, boosting average monthly cheques by $75 for older adults and people with disabilities.

The benefit bump will roll out in January for 72 million Social Security recipients, and on December 31, for nearly 73 million Supplemental Security Income (SSI) beneficiaries.

Starting in 2027, the maximum limit for a taxable wage base, or income cap, is slated to increase to $192,300, up from $184,500 in 2026.

The social security programme is the largest federal social insurance framework in the country. The entitlement programme provides financial support for older adults and disabled people, as well as benefits for survivors of families of workers who have passed away. Funded through dedicated payroll taxes, it serves primarily as a federal pension system that replaces a portion of an individual’s pre-retirement income upon leaving the workforce.

The agency bases the annual increase, closely watched by retirees and others receiving benefits, on the ‌average of the annual increase in the CPI for urban wage earners and clerical workers, also known as the CPI-W index. That index rose 3.9 percent in September and averaged about 3.6 percent for the three months of July, August and September. For 2026, the increase was 2.8 percent.

The announcement comes as high US inflation continues to remain a persistent economic headwind, fuelled primarily by energy shocks from the ongoing wars in Ukraine and Iran, which have caused global energy market turmoil that has sent crude oil prices above $100 a barrel.

More recently, refined petroleum products like diesel fuel have climbed to ‌record highs and have contributed to a widening of inflationary pressures.

Most older adults in the US believe the COLA isn’t adequately keeping up with inflation, according to an AARP poll from September. That poll found that about three-quarters of those 50 or older disagreed with the idea that a 3.5 percent COLA in 2027 would be enough to keep up with rising prices.

articles.title: At least two security officials killed near Iran’s critical Chabahar port
articles.summary: Iran says ‘terrorist groups’ supported from outside the country are targeting security forces.
articles.body:
At least two Iranian security personnel have been killed in separate incidents along the country’s eastern border with Pakistan, adding to a string of attacks near the critical Chabahar port over the past few weeks.

An officer commanding a women’s unit in Iran’s Basij paramilitary force – part of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IGRC) – has been shot and killed outside her home in the Mehrestan district of Sistan-Baluchestan province on Wednesday, according to Tasnim news agency.

Another officer was killed in a separate attack on a police vehicle, also in Mehrestan, which lies close to Iran’s border with Pakistan.

On Wednesday, Haalvash, a rights group focusing on the region’s Baluch ethnic minority in the province, said military helicopters were circling over the city of Iranshahr, adding that the security situation remained tense in several locations.

Iran’s Sistan-Baluchestan province houses the critical Chabahar port on the country’s eastern flank, where US forces carried out air strikes targeting infrastructure and naval control facilities in July.

In recent months, the region has seen multiple attacks staged by groups that Iran’s government says are “terrorist outfits” being funded and supported from outside the country.

Last week, gunmen killed one person and injured three others while attacking a minibus transporting security personnel from a division stationed along the Makran coast, according to the official IRNA news agency.

In a separate incident, IRNA reported that “several terrorists” killed a police officer after attacking a convoy patrolling the area.

Earlier this month, IRGC’s Al Quds Force said it killed at least two suspected attackers and destroyed an alleged “terrorist cell” in an operation near Chabahar port.

The IRGC statement said it had launched the operation after the group killed a member of Iran’s security forces at a checkpoint near the city of Rasak.

IRGC said it had recovered a Starlink device, along with a large quantity of weapons, in the group’s mountainous hideout.

articles.title: Kenya confirms second Ebola case - a relative of the first victim
articles.summary: It follows the death last week of a man who had arrived in Kenya after travelling from DR Congo.
articles.body:
Kenya has confirmed a second case of Ebola, 10 days after a businessman died of the virus after he had travelled to the East African nation from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The new patient, a 39-year-old man, is a close relative of the first case and was already in quarantine when he fell ill on Tuesday, Kenya's health ministry says.

The incubation period for Ebola ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks.

Detecting his illness early had improved his chances of recovery and limited the chance of him passing the virus on to others, the ministry said, as it urged the public to "stay calm but vigilant".

"Both cases are linked, and there is no evidence of spread in the wider community," the ministry said.

"Kenya remains open, with no restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings", it added.

Questions remain over Ebola patient who travelled across three nations undetected

The 40-year-old Kenyan man who died on 5 October was diagnosed with Ebola shortly after being admitted to hospital in the capital, Nairobi.

A relative had taken him there shortly after picking him up at the airport. He had travelled from DR Congo, through Uganda to Kenya without his illness being detected.

Since his death, officials had determined that he had been in contact with 128 people - and since Tuesday 113 of them had been found, the health ministry said.

Of these, 108 were in quarantine in Kenya and tracing of the remaining 15 continued, it said.

More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak to date.

The Ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

"Anyone with fever, unusual tiredness, muscle or joint pains, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding should seek care promptly at the nearest health facility," Kenya's health ministry said.

The current outbreak in DR Congo, which began in May, has been caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.

Shortly after DR Congo declared an outbreak of Ebola in May, it was also reported in Uganda, where two people died.

However, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared that county free of the disease in August.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, the continent's leading public health agency, has reconstructed the Kenyan patient's movements for the six weeks leading up to his death.

It revealed that he first started feeling unwell in DR Congo on 15 September - and showed how several opportunities to detect the infection were missed, including during several visits to Congolese medical facilities.

He then managed to travel through Uganda to Kenya - and was again not detected at airports screenings.

Health experts say it highlights the limitations of relying on temperature checks and self-declarations.

articles.title: Suspected Israeli online operations cause alarm in Iran and Lebanon
articles.summary: Suspected online espionage triggers intense security crackdowns and counter-intelligence measures in Iran and Lebanon.
articles.body:
Israeli intelligence services are believed to be turning to social media to gather information and recruit potential informants in Lebanon and Iran, according to security experts, using online advertisements and appeals tailored to local audiences.

One Instagram account, presenting itself as belonging to Israel’s foreign intelligence agency Mossad, has published Arabic-language messages encouraging people to make contact through confidential channels.

The account, which is verified and operates under the handle @themossad_official, has posted recruitment appeals in colloquial Lebanese Arabic, including inviting people to explore new opportunities by initiating a private conversation.

The profile prominently features pinned highlight reels with Arabic titles such as “Lebanon” displaying a photo of fighters, “Israel”, “Mossad wants you!”, “Protection”, and “Think about your future”.

In August 2025, Lebanon’s General Security Directorate warned residents against interacting with the Instagram account.

In Lebanon, where years of economic turmoil have left many residents facing financial hardship, security officials have warned of suspected Israeli intelligence recruitment efforts involving social media.

In January 2025, the Lebanese newspaper Al Akhbar reported that Israeli intelligence operatives were attempting to recruit Lebanese citizens through fake job advertisements offering high salaries, and through direct outreach on WhatsApp.

Retired Brigadier General Mounir Chehade told the newspaper that the recruitment efforts targeted areas with significant support for Hezbollah, including Beirut’s southern suburbs, southern Lebanon and the Bekaa Valley.

Also in January 2025, Lebanon’s General Security Directorate warned against interacting with a Facebook page called SAWA, which it suspected was a Mossad front aimed at recruiting Lebanese citizens.

Similarly, in December 2025, another Lebanese newspaper L’Orient Today reported that the security agency had warned residents against interacting with a social media page calling itself “Unit 504”.

The page claimed to represent the Israeli military’s human intelligence unit and said it was looking for individuals interested in joining its ranks.

The concerns have been accompanied by arrests of people accused of passing sensitive information to Israel. Lebanese authorities were reported in October 2025 to have previously arrested 32 people suspected of giving information to Israel that was used to target Hezbollah leaders.

Academic and political researcher Wissam Nassif Yassin told Al Jazeera that Israeli intelligence uses colloquial Lebanese Arabic on these platforms to avoid arousing suspicion and to facilitate communication.

“The Israeli side focuses on all segments of society because it considers that every person can be penetrated from their own angle, based on the fact that Hezbollah in Lebanon is integrated into the core of Lebanese society,” Yassin said.

“It focuses on the party’s members primarily, then on the resistance environment secondarily, and on the environment surrounding it thirdly.”

While Israel has had notable sucesses in its intelligence operations in Lebanon – including in gathering information leading to attacks on Hezbollah leaders and members, Yassin argued that collaboration with Israel remained widely rejected in Lebanon.

He also pointed to Hezbollah’s own counterintelligence capabilities, arguing that the group has a long history of identifying and disrupting Israeli intelligence activity.

Yassin pointed to the case of Elhanan Tannenbaum , an alleged Israeli spy who was captured in 2000 after being lured abroad, and was released in 2004 in a prisoner exchange deal.

The use of digital platforms to recruit potential informants also forms part of the longstanding intelligence war between Israel and Iran, which has intensified alongside the military conflict between the two countries.

Hassan Ahmadian, an assistant professor of political science at the University of Tehran, described the current situation as one of the most intense periods in decades-long espionage between the two countries.

“This is an intelligence war. The confrontation between Iran and Israel has continued for decades, but in recent years it has reached its peak,” Ahmadian told Al Jazeera. “Both sides are engaged in intelligence operations. It is an intense conflict that has never stopped.”

Ahmadian said that Israeli recruitment efforts in Iran were sometimes carried out through openly advertised opportunities on social media.

“Israel certainly uses online advertising to recruit people,” he said. “When I was in Iran, I would see advertisements on social media seeking analysts or people to work in security, sometimes offering high salaries and inviting interested applicants to visit a particular page.”

He suggested that openly advertising such opportunities could have a psychological goal beyond recruiting informants, in an attempt to reinforce perceptions of Israel’s intelligence reach inside Iran.

“Israel uses propaganda, but this blatant method is perhaps partly to amplify the Israeli presence,” Ahmadian noted.

The academic also pointed to cases in which Iran had conducted its own counter-operations.

In October 2024, for example, Israeli authorities announced the arrest of seven Israeli nationals accused of spying for Iran by gathering intelligence on military facilities and other sensitive sites.

Separately, the former Israeli Energy Minister Gonen Segev was arrested in 2018 on accusations of spying for Iran. He subsequently pled guilty and was sentenced to 11 years in prison in 2019.

Authorities in Lebanon and Iran have threatened severe penalties for anyone interacting with Israeli accounts.

In July, the Iranian newspaper Kayhan reported that Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence had warned of social media accounts allegedly set up by Mossad to extract information and spread fake news following recent security operations. The ministry claimed that Mossad even offered medical advice to people injured during the United States-Israeli war on Iran, in an attempt to gather sensitive intelligence.

In the same month, the Iranian judiciary also warned that sending images or information to networks deemed to be hostile could result in sentences of 10 to 15 years in prison, heavy fines and potential charges of “corruption on Earth”, which carries the death penalty.

In Lebanon, collaboration with Israel carries a penalty of imprisonment.

As the covert conflict expands online, Ahmadian said that there was little indication that the confrontation would ease.

“I do not expect this intelligence war to stop at any moment between the two parties,” Ahmadian said, “it will remain ongoing and will continue to affect the entire conflict.”

articles.title: Pentagon appoints its own public affairs executive as acting Stars and Stripes publisher
articles.summary: Christian Devine, the Pentagon's public affairs executive director, takes over as acting publisher of Stars and Stripes newspaper as it aims to modernize.
articles.body: The Pentagon has found a new publisher for Stars and Stripes, at least on an interim basis, appointing Christian Devine, executive director of the Pentagon's public affairs office, to lead the military newspaper. Stars and Stripes, which has published a newspaper continuously since World War II, describes itself as a source of "independent news and information to the U.S. military community, including active-duty servicemembers, DoD civilians, veterans, contractors, and their families" that is "governed by the principles of the First Amendment." "The Pentagon is proud to appoint Chris Devine to serve as acting publisher of Stars and Stripes," chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell told Fox News Digital. PENTAGON VOWS TO REFORM MILITARY NEWSPAPER STARS AND STRIPES, REMOVE 'WOKE DISTRACTIONS' "As a former Marine Corps colonel and a seasoned public affairs leader, Chris brings unmatched expertise, strategic vision and a commitment to ensuring Stars and Stripes maintains editorial independence while delivering exclusive, mission-focused reporting that directly serves America’s war fighters and their families," Parnell continued. "In this interim role, he will provide decisive leadership to modernize Stars and Stripes and to strengthen its mission." Devine will continue his role as executive director and principal advisor in the Pentagon’s public affairs office until a permanent Stars and Stripes publisher is found. He is expected to split time between the two gigs. "It’s a dynamic media organization with a prestigious history and purpose, and I hope I can lend a strong arm during the interim to the men and women who continue to contribute to its notable legacy," Devine said in a statement. The Pentagon, which funds roughly half of Stars and Stripes' annual budget, according to the newspaper's website, began 2026 by announcing plans to overhaul the long-running military publication. "The Department of War is returning Stars & Stripes to its original mission: reporting for our warfighters. We are bringing Stars & Stripes into the 21st century. We will modernize its operations, refocus its content away from woke distractions that syphon morale, and adapt it to serve a new generation of service members," Parnell posted on X in January. FIRED STARS AND STRIPES STAFFERS SUE PENTAGON, ALLEGE RETALIATION AND FIRST AMENDMENT VIOLATION "Stars & Stripes will be custom tailored to our warfighters. It will focus on warfighting, weapons systems, fitness, lethality, survivability, and ALL THINGS MILITARY. No more repurposed DC gossip columns; no more Associated Press reprints," Parnell continued. "Stars & Stripes has a proud legacy of reporting news that’s important to our service members. The Department of War is committed to ensuring the outlet continues to reflect that proud legacy." As part of the shake-up, Stars and Stripes' longtime publisher Max Lederer, its editor-in-chief Erik Slavin and Middle East reporter Lara Korte were fired in August. At the time, a source familiar with the matter told Fox News Digital that the firings were a result of Slavin and Korte's unauthorized participation in a "CBS Sunday Morning" segment about the Pentagon's efforts to overhaul the paper and Lederer's refusal to fire them at the direction of Pentagon leadership. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE They have since filed a lawsuit against the Pentagon over their terminations, alleging they are facing "imminent retaliation and termination in violation of their First Amendment and statutory rights." In September, U.S. District Judge Trevor McFadden denied a temporary restraining order filed by Stars and Stripes to reverse their firings, claiming they "ultimately fail to carry their significant burden to show that they are clearly entitled to a preliminary injunction." articles.body: Amid ongoing protests in Delhi over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls, Tamil Nadu’s ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) is set to join the Congress-led INDIA bloc’s campaign against CEC over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter lists.According to news agency PTI, TVK, Congress and other opposition constituents will stage a protest in Chennai on Thursday, October 15.The protest comes amid a widening rift between Congress and the DMK, which has distanced itself from Congress-led agitations and accused its former ally of betrayal.The “protect democracy” agitation will be led by Congress MP B Manickam Tagore, the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) said in a statement. The demonstration is scheduled for 10 am at Ramada Circle on Langs Garden Road in Egmore, with leaders from all seven constituent parties expected to participate.The protest will mark TVK’s first participation in an agitation seeking the CEC’s removal since the party joined the INDIA bloc on October 3, 2026.According to the TNCC, participants will include TVK leader and School Education Minister A Rajmohan, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) president and MP Thol Thirumavalavan, and Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (MDMK) general secretary Vaiko.Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) chief KM Kader Mohideen, Communist Party of India (Marxist) state secretary P Shanmugam, Communist Party of India (CPI) state secretary M Veerapandian, and CPI (Marxist-Leninist) state secretary Pala Asaithamby are also expected to attend. Nivedit Alva, the All India Congress Committee’s in-charge for Tamil Nadu, will be among the Congress functionaries present, the party said.Tagore had earlier described TVK’s entry into the INDIA bloc as “historic”, saying the expansion would strengthen the opposition alliance against the BJP.He had also announced the October 15 demonstration as a joint mobilisation over the SIR and the demand for action against the CEC.DMK skips agitation amid alliance riftThe protest comes amid a widening political rift between the Congress and the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), which said on October 12 that it had exited the INDIA bloc following what it termed a betrayal by the Congress.In a statement, the DMK accused Congress leaders, including Tagore, Girish Chodankar and Praveen Chakravarthy, of making repeated remarks against the Dravidian party while the two parties were allies. It alleged that the Congress had acted as a “sleeper cell of another party” within the DMK-led alliance and blamed the SIR issue and the Congress leaders’ comments for contributing to its electoral defeat.The upcoming protest follows a meeting between Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Vijay on October 10, after TVK joined the INDIA bloc. The two leaders were seen leaving Vijay’s residence together before sharing coffee at Palavakkam.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Washington HS girls blast male athlete participating in track meet: 'Don't think that that's right or fair'
articles.summary: Charlie Garret and Sierra Retzlaff appeared on Fox News' "Fox & Friends" to discuss why they are protesting a male athlete competing in women's cross country events.
articles.body: Charlie Garret and Sierra Retzlaff were among the Washington high school girls who walked away from a cross-country race on Tuesday, refusing to compete against a male athlete who began the season on the boys' team. Instead of bolting off the line when the gun sounded, Garret, Retzlaff and about a dozen other girls walked a few meters and then left the course, while the male athlete took off. "He’s taking that spot. I don’t think that that’s right or fair," Retzlaff said during an appearance on Fox News' "Fox & Friends." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "I agree with Sierra, I don’t think it’s fair at all and he’s taking away a spot from every single girl that lines up on that line," Garret, who appeared on "Fox & Friends" with Retzlaff, said. In addition to walking off, Garret and Retzlaff used body paint to write "keep women in women's sports" on their arms and legs. The male runner finished first in the girls' varsity race on Sept. 29 after finishing 76th in the boys' junior varsity race on Sept. 5. WASHINGTON GIRLS WALK OFF CROSS COUNTRY MEET IN PROTEST OF MALE ATHLETE, PARENTS REVEAL HOW IT CAME TO THIS Garret and Retzlaff both attend Skyview High, while the male runner attends Camas. During Tuesday's race, some members of the male runner's team joined the protest, refusing to compete. "I think it’s amazing what they did and I think it’s really brave and courageous of them," Garret said. "Especially since they are running with this person and is one of their teammates. So, I really applaud those Camas girls, I couldn’t be more proud of them." Retzlaff's parents brought signs supporting their daughter, but her father was removed from the event . The athletic director reportedly said the signs were inappropriate . Although the signs weren't allowed, Retzlaff appreciated her parents' support. DAD BANNED FROM SCHOOL GROUNDS AFTER PROTESTING TRANS RUNNER COMPETING AGAINST HIS DAUGHTER "Obviously it’s great not feeling like you’re the only one doing something and having the people that are always with me through everything really helped a lot," Retzlaff said. Garret said the community as a whole was supportive of their decision to protest, even if their team was a little shocked at first. The Camas School District said it follows Washington Interscholastic Activities Association eligibility rules and Washington state law, but an upcoming vote could change the policy. On Nov. 3, Washington voters will vote on Initiative 638, which would prohibit students defined as biologically male from competing in certain female-only interscholastic athletic competitions. The initiative would require students to provide verification of biological sex from a healthcare provider to enter those competitions. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD However, even if the initiative is approved, it would not take effect in time for Garret, Retzlaff and the other protesting girls. Washington's state cross-country championships are scheduled for Nov. 7, and the measure would go into effect 30 days after the election. OutKick's Jackson Thompson contributed to this report.

articles.title: In 1991, California’s Oakland fire left 1,272 pets affected; researchers found that ID collars made pets more than 10 times as likely to be reunited with their owners
articles.summary: The 1991 Oakland fire highlighted the importance of pet identification, revealing that animals with ID collars were significantly more likely to be reunited with their owners. Discover the lasting lessons from this disaster for pet owners today.
articles.body: When a wildfire tears through a neighbourhood, people may have only minutes to get out. Pets may flee in panic, hide in unfamiliar places, or become separated from their owners during evacuations. Even after the flames are extinguished, finding these animals can take weeks or months. A fire that swept through Oakland, California, in October 1991 showed how a collar with an owner’s name and address could greatly improve a pet’s chances of getting home.According to a 1998 study published in the Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association, the 1991 Oakland fire left many cats and dogs missing, abandoned or roaming without their owners. Researchers analysed records for 1,075 cats and 197 dogs affected by the fire. They found that pets wearing collars with their owners’ names and addresses were more than ten times as likely to be reunited with their families as pets without collars.A fire left hundreds of pets without their ownersThe fire erupted on 19 October 1991 and quickly spread in the Oakland-Berkeley hills. Most people were away from home when the fire struck, and road closures and evacuation restrictions made it hard for many to return and collect their pets. Some pets escaped, while others were left behind in the chaos. The study evaluated data collected by the Oakland Firestorm Pet Hotline between 1991 and 1995. The study sample included 1,075 cats and 197 dogs affected by the fire, for a total of 1,272 pets. The researchers also evaluated data from 221 cats and 128 dogs that were not affected by the disaster.The hotline did more than take phone calls; it also recorded reports of missing and found animals. Most of the animals found after the disaster were either stray pets or animals already living ferally in the area. Some animals remained missing, and the researchers assumed they had died in the disaster. It was therefore difficult to determine whether all the animals recorded as found had been separated from their families by the fire. Research states that the hotline activity peaked on the third and fourth days after the disaster, before calls declined and levelled off by the 21st day.The simple collar that made a remarkable differenceThe study produced several findings, but one stood out. Animals wearing collars with their owners’ names and addresses were more than ten times as likely to be reunited with their owners as animals without collars. The reason is straightforward. A pet may be found by a passerby or rescuer who can identify the owner only from the tag.Identification alone did not guarantee a reunion. The longer owners waited to search, the less likely they were to reunite with their pets. After the disaster, time mattered because animals could wander off or be adopted before owners found them. Nevertheless, the results sent a clear message to pet owners. Pets should be identified before a disaster, because there may be no time to do it afterwards. A collar with current contact information can help a finder reach the owner quickly.Why the lesson still mattersThe Oakland fire highlighted the difficulties of reuniting animals with their owners during an emergency. Some animals were adopted by the people who found them, particularly those discovered near the fire zone. The incident also underlined the importance of pet identification, both in everyday life and during disasters.Collars and tags can help rescuers identify a pet quickly, although they may become lost or detached. Microchips provide an additional means of identification, provided the animal is scanned and the registered contact details are up to date. Using both visible identification and a registered microchip therefore offers a more reliable way to reconnect lost pets with their owners.As the Oakland study drew on records from a single disaster, its findings should not be assumed to apply equally to every fire or evacuation. Nevertheless, the practical lesson remains relevant: clear, accessible identification can improve the chances of reuniting lost animals with their families, particularly when an emergency separates them.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ex-UK army chef jailed for ‘terror’-related offence
articles.summary: The former British Army member harboured ‘extreme right-wing’ views and was ordering explosives components, say police.
articles.body:
A British court has handed a former army chef a nearly four-year jail term for possessing weapons for “terrorist purposes”.

Mark Broadhurst, 28, was given the sentence on Wednesday at Sheffield Crown Court in England, two years after police uncovered online messages in which he expressed racist views and an intention to sell homemade firearms to right-wing groups.

Police found a stockpile of weapons at Broadhurst’s home address when they took him into custody in September 2024, including knives and crossbows, black powder, ammunition, air pistols and what officials described as “an improvised homemade cannon”.

The former British Army member was also found to be part of an online chat group with three other men who last year were jailed for planning to carry out a “terrorist” attack at mosques or synagogues as part of what they believed to be a coming “race war”.

Frank Ferguson, head of the special crime division of the UK’s public prosecution agency, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), said Broadhurst was “clearly interested in violence and developing weapons that had the ability to cause untold harm to innocent people”.

Detective Chief Superintendent James Dunkerley, who heads “counterterror” policing in the northeastern region, said Broadhurst was found to be harbouring an “extreme right-wing mindset” and was “proactively ordering components to make explosives”.

Broadhurst pleaded guilty to firearm possession and possessing an explosive under suspicious circumstances, but denied they were for “terrorism” purposes. ⁠A judge, however, ruled that Broadhurst’s offences were connected to “terrorism”.

His conviction comes against a backdrop of rising racial tensions and hate crimes in the UK, with marginalised communities increasingly targeted.

British police in July arrested 12 people in connection with an “extreme right-wing terrorism threat” targeting an Islamic gathering in eastern England.

Six months earlier, UK prosecutors said they were handling the highest number of hate crime cases referred by police in its history.

articles.title: Airport drop-off charges to be reviewed after sharp increase
articles.summary: Confirming the review, the government said it was "vital to ensure travel remains accessible and that passengers are treated fairly".
articles.body:
Airport drop-off charges are to be reviewed by the government following sharp price increases in recent years.

Prices at major airports have risen by a third since the summer of 2025 on average, according to one analysis, with Gatwick and Stansted drop-off charges found to be the most expensive, jumping from £7 to £10.

Such charges at Edinburgh Airport have risen from £6 to £8.50, while fees at Bournemouth increased from £5 to £8, the same price as Leeds Bradford and London City.

The Department for Transport confirmed it had committed to a review, saying it was "vital to ensure travel remains accessible and that passengers are treated fairly".

The government added it hoped airports would "exercise restraint on rises, particularly where there are limited public transport alternatives".

The RAC, which conducted the analysis in July this year, has campaigned against increases in drop-off charges. It said a review of "kiss and fly" fees would be "music to the ears to drivers".

"We know airport drop-off charges are a growing source of anger and frustration," said Rod Dennis, senior policy officer at the RAC.

"Four-in-five drivers we've surveyed believe they are a 'rip-off', with just one-in-10 understanding why airports charge what they do."

The RAC's research found London City Airport, which only introduced charges in 2026, was the most expensive on a per-minute basis.

Its £8 charge for five minutes works out at £1.60 per minute. Belfast International Airport now charges £5 for 10 minutes in the drop-off zone, up £2 on last year.

None of the top 10 airports in the European Union charge for drop-offs, according to the RAC.

It argues that international airports should not charge for dropping off passengers, however, the industry said the charges were a neccesary part of the business model of airports.

Airport drop-off fees up by a third - here are the priciest

Supporters of such charges also say they encourage travellers to use of more environmentally friendly modes of transport.

"Airports outside the UK are typically publicly owned and in receipt of state subsidies and tax exemptions, while UK airports are generally privately owned and subject to the full array of commercial rates of taxation," said Karen Dee, chief executive of Airports UK, which represents airports.

She added airports offered a "range of options for those travelling to terminals, including free drop off points" and that "any review" by the government would find airports make "excellent use of a variety of ways to manage traffic and air pollution".

The Aviation Environment Federation campaign group has previously defended the fees, arguing they help reduce congestion and air pollution around airports.

Earlier this month, the government announced extra charges for parents sitting with their children when flying would be scrapped in time for next year's summer holidays.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the changes were part of a series of "everyday fixes" to ease cost of living pressures on households.

articles.title: In India, engineers coated road aggregate with shredded plastic before adding bitumen; an NH-207 test track reported satisfactory performance
articles.summary: Engineers in India have successfully tested a road construction method using shredded waste plastic coated on stone aggregate before adding bitumen, demonstrating satisfactory performance on a 20-kilometre test track on National Highway 207 in Karnataka.
articles.body: Engineers in India tested a road-building method that uses shredded waste plastic to coat heated stone aggregate before bitumen is added, and one of the major field trials was carried out on National Highway 207 in Karnataka, where a 20-kilometre test section compared several modified bituminous binders, including a waste-plastic formulation. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways later described the waste-plastic section as showing satisfactory performance.The process tested in India is known as the dry process, in which shredded plastic is added to hot aggregate, where it coats the surface of the stone. Hot bitumen is added to the plastic-coated aggregate after, before the mixture is laid and compacted as pavement.The NH-207 test compared five pavement bindersThe R-85 research project was commissioned by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and carried out by the Indian Institute of Technology Madras, with engineers constructing a 20-kilometre test track on NH-207 between Devanahalli and Doddaballapur in Karnataka in 2010. The test section was divided among five types of binder, which were conventional VG-30, SBS-modified binder, crumb-rubber-modified binder, natural-rubber-modified binder and waste-plastic-modified binder.The researchers monitored the sections after construction and collected field-performance data alongside laboratory measurements, and the work examined properties such as pavement roughness, deflection and the behavior of the different mixes under traffic and environmental conditions. The waste-plastic section was therefore a part of a highway test track where different modified binders were placed in actual pavement and monitored over time.Plastic was added before the bitumenProcessed plastic is shredded to a controlled size and introduced to heated aggregate under the method described by India's road authorities, with the plastic softening and forming a coating around the stone before hot bitumen is added. Government guidance specifies controls over the plastic used in the process, since the material has to be cleaned and shredded within specified size limits, and the plastic must have a suitable melting point so it can coat the aggregate during mixing. The guidance also sets temperature controls because excessive heating can cause thermal degradation.The approach was developed around waste plastics that could otherwise require disposal, and was not intended to put every type of plastic into asphalt. India's technical guidance makes the distinction between plastics that can be used in the dry process and materials that are unsuitable.Field tests preceded national guidelinesThe NH-207 work was completed before India formally issued its first national guidelines for using waste plastic in hot bituminous wearing courses, and the Indian Roads Congress published IRC SP:98:2013 after laboratory and field studies conducted in India. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways encouraged the use of waste plastic on national highways within 50 kilometres of qualifying urban areas and required pilot stretches to assess performance.A 2019 government statement said that waste plastic had already been used in the wearing course of about 50 kilometres of national highway stretches and that projects of at least 10 kilometres were to be taken up as pilots for performance assessment. The government's approach therefore moved from field trials toward specifications and wider deployment, and the NH-207 project was one part of that evidence base. Its importance was not that one test track immediately changed India's road policy, but that engineers had actual highway-performance data to evaluate alongside laboratory studies before plastic-modified pavement became part of national road guidance.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1995, chef Alice Waters started the Edible Schoolyard at a Berkeley middle school; 31 years later, its network connects more than 5,800 food-and-garden education programs across 75 countries
articles.summary: What began as a small project in a neglected schoolyard in California has grown into an international movement that teaches children about food, gardening
articles.body: What began as a small project in a neglected schoolyard in California has grown into an international movement that teaches children about food, gardening and the environment. The Edible Schoolyard Project was founded in 1995 by chef and food activist Alice Waters. Today, it connects more than 5,800 garden and food education programmes across 75 countries and 53 US states and territories. According to the Edible Schoolyard Network registry, the project has grown from a single school garden in Berkeley, California, into a worldwide network of school gardens, classrooms and food education programmes.Transforming concrete into living classroomsThe project began when Waters, who founded the well-known Chez Panisse restaurant and previously worked as a Montessori teacher, passed Martin Luther King Jr. Middle School in Berkeley. She noticed an overgrown plot of land and a school kitchen that was no longer in use. Working with school leaders, teachers and local residents, Waters started a project to turn the unused asphalt area into an organic garden. She also helped reopen the kitchen so students could learn about food through practical lessons. According to the project's official documents, the aim was not just to teach children how to grow plants. It was to make food education a regular part of their schoolwork. "To spend time in an Edible Schoolyard is to realize how much more is going on here than teaching kids how to garden or cook," wrote author and food journalist Michael Pollan in a statement published on the organisation's website. "Kids begin to learn about food in all its dimensions, as an edible medium of culture, science, ecology, and even social justice."Integrating academics with practical skillsAt the original Berkeley site, students take part in planting, harvesting and cooking as part of their regular school timetable. These activities help them learn practical skills while studying familiar academic subjects. Teachers connect garden work to lessons in science, history and mathematics. In science classes, students learn about soil and how compost breaks down. History lessons explore where crops originated and how they spread through trade. Mathematics activities include measuring garden plots and adjusting recipes to serve different numbers of people. According to curriculum guides published by the organisation, this hands-on approach helps students think more carefully about farming, public health and the environment. It also encourages healthy eating habits among teenagers. By linking classroom lessons with activities in the garden and kitchen, the programme gives students a chance to see how what they learn at school applies to everyday life.A global network of food educationOver the past 31 years, the model has spread well beyond California. Public and private educational institutions in many countries have adopted food and garden education programmes inspired by the project. The Edible Schoolyard Network database includes a wide range of initiatives. These include primary school gardens in Italy, goat dairies in Grenada and community farming spaces in Stockton, California. The network's online platform allows teachers, programme leaders and volunteers to share free teaching materials, exchange advice on running their projects and locate garden-based learning initiatives around the world. According to the project's annual reports, each participating site runs its activities according to local conditions, including climate, available funding and community needs. However, all the programmes share a central goal: helping students learn through practical activities involving food. This flexible approach allows schools and communities to adapt the model to their own needs while keeping its main educational purpose intact.Institutional influence and future directionThe movement has also helped encourage changes in how schools approach food and meals. In Berkeley, early successes with the project contributed to wider changes in the school district's meal programme. These efforts helped lay the groundwork for universal breakfast initiatives and greater use of food from local farmers. The project has consistently stressed that children's wellbeing involves more than academic achievement. Its approach connects food, education and the environment, while encouraging schools to treat students with care and respect. In an official profile published on the project's platform, Waters described the principles behind the organisation's work. "Our vision is grounded in the key principle that children deserve to be nurtured in body and mind, treated with dignity, and shown that they are valued," Waters stated in an official profile released by the project. As the network continues to connect thousands of programmes around the world, its organisers remain focused on making practical food and environmental education a regular part of children's schooling. The project that began with an unused schoolyard and kitchen in Berkeley has grown into a wider effort to help students understand where food comes from, how it affects their health and how growing and preparing it can become part of their education.aYou use AI every day. articles.title: Kamala Harris calls to expand Supreme Court, add states if Dems take Congress
articles.summary: Kamala Harris called for Supreme Court expansion and Electoral College changes, and a legal expert warned her proposals could set a dangerous precedent.
articles.body: Former Vice President Kamala Harris called for institutional changes to the Supreme Court and the Electoral College during an interview Tuesday, calling for more justices on the highest court in the nation. "The work that we can do about winning back the House and the Senate is going to be on a number of things. For example, I believe that we need to expand the Supreme Court. We need more justices on the Supreme Court so that we can have a court that actually reinforces the spirit and principles behind the Constitution of the United States," Harris told podcast host Keke Palmer on her "Baby, This is Keke Palmer" podcast. "I believe that we should be pushing for what is possible around changing the Electoral College. Right? "It's about, the popular vote has to matter, right? You know, all the things that make people feel, like, overwhelmed, and does their vote matter? We have, you know, listen, if the folks there want it, we should be pushing for statehood for Puerto Rico and D.C., right? These are some of the things that are structural that we need to do, but we need to reestablish affordable child care," Harris added. KAMALA HARRIS FACES DEMOCRATIC DOUBTS OVER 2028 AS ALLIES PUSH BACK ON CLAIMS SHE’S SQUANDERED HER CHANCE Harris lost both the Electoral College and the popular vote to President Donald Trump in 2024. She told Palmer she still remains undecided about a 2028 presidential run. Y. David Scharf, chairman of Morrison Cohen LLP and head of its government strategies & controversies practice, told Fox News Digital that Harris' proposed changes could set a "dangerous precedent." "Kamala Harris says she wants to defend democracy, but her solution is to rewrite its rules when Democrats don't like the results. That's a dangerous precedent," he said. "Nine justices have been the number since 1869. FDR tried to pack the Supreme Court, and even his own party pushed back. Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg herself warned that expanding the court would make it look partisan. GAVIN NEWSOM EXPRESSES 'OPENNESS' TO PACKING SCOTUS, CALLS ELECTORAL COLLEGE SYSTEM 'PERVERTED' "The Electoral College is written into the Constitution. Eliminating it requires a constitutional amendment, not a Democratic majority in Congress. You don't get to change the referee because you don't like the calls. Harris may think this is a winning message for the Democratic base, but it's a much tougher sell to the independent and swing voters her party needs." The former VP also spoke about the midterm elections during the interview. "On the first Tuesday in November, the midterms are going to happen," Harris said. "And our ability to put people in Congress who will say no, when they do things like cut $1 trillion out of Medicaid will be powerful and affect people right away. "Our ability to put people in Congress who will say enough of the corruption, enough of ending the funding for research on issues like fibroids, which they have done under the guise of attacking DEI, can be stopped. There are things that are not only about what will be helpful, but also stopping what is harmful, that we can do right away with these midterm elections." Her comments come days after her 2024 vice presidential running mate, Gov. Tim Walz, warned of a reckoning among Democrats if the party fails to deliver on promises should they take back Congress and potentially the presidency in 2028. Harris was called out by Democratic advisors Tuesday for failing to reinvent herself politically as she weighs another White House run, Politico reported. The report, based on interviews with nearly 20 California-based Democratic donors and strategists, highlighted growing skepticism among some party insiders about Harris' political future and whether she has done enough to distinguish herself from her unsuccessful 2024 campaign. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Longtime Democratic strategist Doug Herman, a veteran of former President Barack Obama’s 2008 and 2012 campaigns, told Politico that Harris "totally blew it. … She hasn’t gotten into the mix." Former Gov. Jim Hodges of South Carolina, the leadoff state in the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nominating calendar, told the outlet, "I don’t see anything different myself. It seems like more of the same to me." Veteran Democratic strategist Maria Cardona, an outside advisor to Harris, pushed back against the criticism highlighted in a new Politico report and called the story "infuriating" in a previous statement to Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "How can you state that she hasn’t done anything new or groundbreaking or talked about new initiatives or policies and then lay out exactly those policies — like proposing an expanded Supreme Court, lowering the voting age to 16, making D.C. and Puerto Rico states. Those are pretty groundbreaking policies," Cardona told Fox News Digital, as she pointed to some of Harris' moves since the end of former President Joe Biden's administration.

articles.title: In 1968, a London buyer paid £45 for a painting in a junk shop because he suspected it might be special; experts later confirmed it as a Van Gogh, and in 2020 the work sold for about €12 million to €15 million
articles.summary: A painting bought for just £45 from a London junk shop in 1968 went on to become a multimillion-euro artwork after experts confirmed that it was an
articles.body: A painting bought for just £45 from a London junk shop in 1968 went on to become a multimillion-euro artwork after experts confirmed that it was an original by Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh. The painting, titled Peasant Woman in front of a Farmhouse, was sold to a private collector for approximately €12 million to €15 million at the TEFAF Maastricht art fair in the Netherlands in March 2020.The buyer who first recognised its possible value was Luigi Grosso, an Italian working for the BBC, The Art Newspaper reported. He came across the painting in a shop in Belsize Park, north London, and noticed that it carried the signature “Vincent” in the lower left corner. While the shopkeeper believed it belonged to an artist with that surname, Grosso suspected that it could be an original Van Gogh.His decision to buy the painting for £45 proved significant. With help from art curator Alan Bowness, who had organised an exhibition of Van Gogh's work at London's Hayward Gallery, Grosso arranged for the painting to be authenticated. It was subsequently sold at Sotheby's in New York in 1970 for $110,000.The artwork had spent decades at a farm in Staffordshire, where it was once stored in an attic and eventually sold for only £4.How a Van Gogh painting ended up at a farmThe painting, created in July 1885, is known in French as Paysanne devant une chaumière. Before entering the art market, it had been kept at Billington Farm, just outside Stafford in England.According to the Holme family, who owned the farm, John Holme (1871–1952) received the painting in 1929 as payment for a debt involving agricultural supplies. Rather than receiving money for the supplies, he accepted the artwork.The painting remained at the property for several decades. It initially hung inside the farmhouse but was later moved to the attic when the family grew tired of displaying it.In 1967, John's son Charles sold the painting during a general farm sale after retiring. It fetched just £4, with its connection to Van Gogh still unrecognised.The following year, the artwork appeared in a London shop, where Grosso noticed it and decided to investigate its possible origins.How Grosso discovered painting In September 1968, Grosso visited a shop in Belsize Park that he later described to art writer Martin Bailey as somewhere between a junk shop and an antiques dealer.The painting caught his attention because of the signature and its appearance. Although the shop owner did not believe it was a work by the famous Dutch artist, Grosso knew enough about art to consider the possibility.He purchased it for £45 and sought help from Alan Bowness, who had recently curated a Van Gogh exhibition at the Hayward Gallery.With Bowness's assistance, the painting was authenticated as a genuine work by Van Gogh. The confirmation changed its position in the art market.In 1970, Grosso offered the painting at Sotheby's in New York. Hollywood film producer Joseph Levine bought it for $110,000, marking a substantial increase from the amount Grosso had paid two years earlier.Painting changed owners several timesAfter acquiring the painting, Levine kept it until 1983, when it returned to Sotheby's in New York. This time, it sold for $390,000 to Roberto Polo, a Cuban-born American art collector.Polo owned the painting for approximately two years before selling it at Sotheby's in London in 1985. A collector from Montreal purchased it for £264,000.The artwork changed hands again in 2001, when it appeared at Sotheby's in New York for a fourth time. It sold for $1.7 million to an American collector.Despite appearing at several major auctions, the painting was rarely displayed in institutional exhibitions.s only institutional exhibition loan was to London's Royal Academy of Arts in 2010.Sold for up to €15 million in 2020In March 2020, the painting returned to the international art market through London-based gallery Dickinson, which exhibited it at TEFAF Maastricht in the Netherlands.The gallery agreed to sell the work to a private collector for approximately €12 million to €15 million, equivalent to around $13.5 million to $16.9 million at the time. articles.title: Middlemen demand fee for house regularisation in Kothagudem
articles.summary: Telangana GO 76 house regularisation restarts in Kothagudem; middlemen allegedly demand ₹2,000–₹3,000/sq yd for title deeds; officials warn against scams.
articles.body: Hyderabad: With the Telangana govt restarting the process of regularising houses under GO No. 76, middlemen in Kothagudem have allegedly begun approaching applicants, promising to secure title deeds for a price of up to ₹3,000 per square yard for commercial plots and ₹2,000 for residential properties. They are reportedly assuring house owners that they can get the deeds issued by influencing officials, even without waiting for the prescribed survey and verification process to be completed.The regularisation process, which had stalled before the assembly elections, has now resumed, bringing fresh hope to thousands of applicants who have been waiting for ownership documents. The govt has given the green signal to issue title deeds to 2,200 applicants who had submitted applications earlier, and a survey has begun in Kothagudem.However, the resumption of the process has also created an opportunity for middlemen to target applicants anxious to secure their property rights. According to the rates being quoted by these intermediaries, regularising a 100-square-yard commercial plot could cost an applicant around ₹3 lakh, while a residential plot of the same size could cost ₹2 lakh. The middlemen are allegedly claiming that they can ensure the work gets done by arranging matters with officials.Some local political leaders are also alleged to be attempting to use the regularisation process to recover their political expenditure. They are reportedly identifying applicants through intermediaries and negotiating how the money collected would be shared.The alleged arrangement involves dividing the applicants among different intermediaries, with each seeking to secure a share of the money paid by those hoping to obtain title deeds. The claims have raised concerns about applicants being pressured to pay for a process that is supposed to be carried out under govt rules.In one instance reported from Pragathi Nagar, a house owner who had applied for a title deed earlier was approached by a middleman after the survey resumed. The intermediary allegedly demanded ₹1 lakh, promising to deliver the registration deed directly to the applicant’s house.“The middleman assured me that the deed could be secured without depending on the survey process. However, I refused, saying the amount was beyond my means, following which the intermediary left,” said the applicant on condition of anonymity.The incident highlights how applicants waiting for official confirmation of their property rights could be vulnerable to such promises, particularly when they are uncertain about the timeline and outcome of the regularisation process.Kothagudem tahsildar Pullaiah said the distribution of title deeds would be conducted transparently and strictly in accordance with the prescribed rules.“There is no scope for middlemen to interfere in the process. People should not trust such persons or waste their money. The process will be carried out officially, following the rules, and applicants should remain alert,” he said.Officials have cautioned applicants against paying anyone who claims to have influence over the process or promises to secure title deeds outside the prescribed procedure. articles.title: Just because the witness is victim’s relative, it is no ground to disbelieve, says Calcutta High Court
articles.summary: Calcutta High Court upholds life term in 2009 rape-murder of 11-year-old; says victim’s relatives’ testimony can’t be disbelieved; orders Rs 4 lakh compensation.
articles.body: Kolkata: The Calcutta High Court on Wednesday upheld the life term of a convict in the rape and murder of an 11-year-old girl, whose body was found hanging from a mango orchard in Feb 2009, observing that just because a witness was the victim’s relative it was no ground to disbelieve them.The division bench of Justice Rajasekhar Mantha and Justice Anuj Singh directed the state to pay Rs 4 lakh to the victim’s parents, who “suffered as a result of the crime”, within seven days. The court said the state could recover the compensation amount from the convict.Yeasin Sk was convicted on May 20, 2015, and was sentenced to life for murder and 10 years for rape of the 11-year-old girl. The incident occurred on Feb 1, 2009, in Murshidabad, when the girl was on her way to her grandmother’s place. Yeasin kidnapped her, took her to a mango orchard on a bicycle, raped her and murdered her. Meanwhile, the victim’s parents did not search for her as they thought she had reached her grandmother’s house, while the grandmother thought she never left her parents’ home. It was the next morning that some persons, passing by the mango orchard, noticed the victim’s body hanging. They informed the victim’s father, who along with his wife and others, reached the orchard to find their daughter’s half-clad body hanging from the wooden ceiling of a tin shed.Two prosecution witnesses said they had seen the victim speak to Yeasin and another youth, Royal Sk, and charges were framed against both but the latter was acquitted.The victim’s grandmother claimed that one of the witnesses, Gobindo Sheikh, saw the victim being taken away by Yeasin on a red bicycle. The victim’s mother, too, said she had seen her daughter speaking to Yeasin at a tea stall. One of the witnesses, who saw the victim being dragged by the convict, told the parents later that he saw Yeasin take the sobbing child to the orchard.Yeasin’s lawyer’s case was that the two witnesses, who had said they had seen the convict take the child on a bicycle, had turned hostile. “The court must carefully scrutinise the evidence of a hostile witness before rejecting it. The retraction of a witness during a trial could be dealt with by scrutinising the evidence of other witnesses, who confirmed that the hostile witness previously shared the retracted facts with them,” it was submitted. But the division bench took into account the aspect of “economic and social factors” that could also cause a witness to resign from their previous statement. The court said the accused often frightened witnesses, forcing them to move away from the truth. So, a hostile witness’s evidence could not simply be discarded. The other argument was as the witnesses were closely related to the victim, they were interested witnesses. “A witness’s evidence cannot be brushed aside on the grounds that he is a relative of the victim… An interested witness is one who derives a benefit or settles personal scores from the conviction of an accused. A victim’s family member deposes about the assailant. Thus, a related witness cannot be conflated with an interested witness,” the bench noted.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Jharkhand explores REDD+ road map to secure climate finance
articles.summary: Jharkhand explores a REDD+ road map to cut deforestation, conserve carbon-rich forests, ensure community rights, and access results-based climate finance.
articles.body: Ranchi: Jharkhand has begun exploring a state-specific road map under the global REDD+ framework to access results-based climate finance while strengthening forest conservation, biodiversity protection and community livelihoods.The proposal was discussed at a high-level meeting chaired by principal chief conservator of forests Sanjiv Kumar on Wednesday. Senior forest officials, researchers and experts attended the meeting.Jharkhand has 23,765.78 sq km of forest cover, accounting for 29.81% of its geographical area. Its forests are estimated to store 186.43 million tonnes of carbon, giving the state significant potential to develop a REDD+ programme focused on forest protection, carbon conservation, ecological restoration and livelihood generation.Kumar said the proposed initiative would aim to reduce deforestation and forest degradation, conserve carbon-rich sal forests and wildlife habitats, promote sustainable forest management, and restore degraded landscapes through natural regeneration and bamboo-based plantations.However, the programme faces several challenges, including the need to establish credible carbon baselines, develop robust monitoring systems, create transparent benefit-sharing mechanisms and safeguard community rights under the Forest Rights Act and the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act or PESA.Kumar said community rights, participation and benefit-sharing mechanisms must be incorporated from the planning stage to ensure that REDD+ interventions are socially legitimate and sustainable. He added that the programme should recognise the rights and customary dependence of forest-dwelling communities under applicable laws and policies.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news.
